content:
emma (support): FYI incoming escalation from Acme. Their hosted inference requests started returning 504s ~16:03 UTC, multiple customers affected. They report full request timeouts and a backlog on our gateway logs. :rotating_light:

raj (eng-sre): Can you paste the gateway logs + request ids? First suspicion is scale-up lag combined with model init timeouts.

emma (support): Pasting snippets from gateway and k8s: 
```
[16:03:12] gateway ERROR upstream_timeout request_id=acme-req-9f3
[16:03:13] proxy 504 "POST /v1/generate" 120533ms
```
And from keda-bot: 
```
[keda-bot] scaledobject my-model-scaler observed 0 active replicas -> scale to 0 (minReplicaCount=0)
[keda-bot] cooldown 300s
```
Also Deployment pods show CrashLoop for the first 90s while model downloads.

miguel (oncall): Confirming from nodes: cluster autoscaler didn't add nodes because cluster reached max nodes in pool (autoscaler max=5). HPA / KEDA didn't spin up new pods fast enough; new pods stuck in ContainerCreating then Ready=false due to readinessProbe failing while model download runs ~100-130s. Gateway timeout is 60s, so requests hit 504.

sarah (eng-runtime): This is a classic cold-start vs readiness mismatch. Our model server endpoint /health becomes ready only after weights loaded (~120s). ReadinessProbe was configured with initialDelaySeconds=10 and timeoutSeconds=1 -> Kubernetes considers pod not ready (expected), but because KEDA minReplicas=0 and HPA relies on ready replicas, the scaler's metric (queue length) triggered but scale-to-zero + cooldown caused delay. We should either keep warm replicas or make readiness faster.

olivia (customer-success): Customer is furious; they saw a spike of 5xxs across multiple apps and opened a support ticket. They asked for immediate mitigation and postmortem.

raj (eng-sre): Immediate mitigation steps I pushed: 
- kubectl patch scaledobject my-model-scaler --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":2}}' to force 2 warm pods
- patched gateway to increase upstream timeout to 180s for that route
- requested quota bump on node pool from infra for +3 nodes

Command I ran: 
```
kubectl patch scaledobject my-model-scaler -n hosted --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":2}}'
kubectl -n hosted set env deployment/model-deploy GATEWAY_MAX_TIMEOUT=180
```
Result: new pods started and began model init, requests gradually recovered around 16:12 UTC.

emma (support): Customer confirmed partial recovery at 16:13, but still seeing intermittent 502s for long generations. They're asking for root cause and permanent fix.

sarah (eng-runtime): Proposed long-term fixes: 
1) Add a StartupProbe that checks model-ready and set higher failure threshold vs readiness, so kube knows pods are initializing rather than failing; make readiness only true after model-ready endpoint. 
2) Change KEDA ScaledObject minReplicaCount to >0 for heavy models OR implement a warm-pool controller that keeps N containers preloaded. 
3) Tune cluster-autoscaler max & scale-up buffer for high-traffic tenants (or use reserved node pools per-account). 
4) Implement a quick-return path at gateway: if model backend is 'initializing' return 202+Retry-After instead of proxying and waiting to timeout.

sarah (eng-runtime): Example StartupProbe snippet to add: 
```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /model/ready
    port: 8080
  failureThreshold: 30  # allows ~150s init
  periodSeconds: 5
```
Readiness becomes simple /model/ready check but StartupProbe prevents kube from killing pod during long download.

raj (eng-sre): Also found KEDA config had a long cooldown (300s) + polling interval 30s that slowed re-scaling. Suggest lowering cooldown to 60s and polling to 10s for this scaler.

miguel (oncall): Opened incident ticket INC-2026 and assigned follow-ups: 
- eng-sre to evaluate KEDA tuning and minReplica defaults (owner: raj)
- eng-runtime to add StartupProbe and recommend warm-pool pattern (owner: sarah)
- infra to review nodepool autoscaler max & burst capacity (owner: miguel)
Estimated timeline for fixes: quick config changes today; code changes in 1-2 sprints.

olivia (customer-success): I told Acme we'll provide a detailed postmortem and a timeline for mitigations. They asked for log extract and prometheus graphs — attaching in ticket.

deploy-bot: canary deployment of model-server v2.1 passed health checks (no traffic routed yet).

emma (support): Repro steps for QA env I used to reproduce locally: 
1) Set minReplicaCount=0 on ScaledObject and cooldown=300s
2) Use large model (weights ~1.2GB) that has ~110s init on small GPU
3) Send concurrent burst of 50 requests -> observe gateway 504s when cluster has scale-limits
Commands: 
```
# emulate load
ab -n 50 -c 10 -p payload.json https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate
```
Observations: request latency climbs, scaler signals scale but pods are NotReady for ~2 minutes, gateway times out at 60s.

raj (eng-sre): Follow-ups: 
- add test harness to simulate cold-start bursts in CI so we don't regress.
- default our heavy-model ScaledObjects to minReplicaCount=1 unless explicitly allowed to scale-to-zero.

sarah (eng-runtime): We should also expose a lighter-weight health endpoint that returns initializing+progress so gateway can return 202 and user gets clearer message.

miguel (oncall): For the immediate postmortem I'll collect timelines, prometheus alert history (keda scaler, hpa, node autoscaler), and pod events. Will tag back with owner PRs.

emma (support): Thanks all — customer notified of mitigations. Closing slack thread for now; will update when postmortem lands. :white_check_mark:
